name: Florida Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Cuban, Seafood & More
description:
Florida's restaurants, and the Cuban sandwiches, stone crabs and oyster bars worth the drive.

Florida Eats is a free guide to eating in Florida: 252 places on hand-checked guides (Cuban sandwiches and coffee windows, stone crabs, grouper and seafood shacks, Keys classics, oyster bars, fish camps, Latin and Caribbean kitchens and the state's oldest restaurants), MICHELIN and James Beard honorees, and 52,573 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 596 towns. No account, no ads.

FLORIDA GUIDES
• Cuban & Cafecito: Cuban sandwiches, bakeries and ventanitas, from Calle Ocho to Ybor City.
• Stone Crabs: in season Oct 15 – May 1.
• Grouper & Seafood Shacks: grouper sandwiches on the Gulf and Atlantic.
• Keys Classics: key lime pie, conch fritters and Keys seafood.
• Oyster Bars and Fish Camps & Smoked Fish: raw bars, Old Florida fish camps and smoked fish dip.
• Latin & Caribbean: Haitian, Venezuelan, Colombian, Puerto Rican and more.
• MICHELIN & James Beard: the MICHELIN Guide Florida 2026 selection and James Beard honorees, as facts.
• Oldest Places: founding years checked at the same address, oldest first.

THE STATE'S OWN INSPECTIONS
Florida's Division of Hotels and Restaurants inspects the restaurants it licenses. 48,584 licensed places show the state's result at their latest visit, in the state's own words, with the date and its violation counts. Florida doesn't grade restaurants, and neither does this app.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "cuban sandwich tampa", "stone crab", "southwest 8th street".
• Filter by town or cuisine, hide chains.
• Save places for your next trip.
• Find hand-checked and honored places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on a place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every place in the Florida guides was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source: the place's own website or menu, local news or an official tourism listing. Restaurants come from the State of Florida's food service licenses (DBPR) and Overture Maps open data. Website links are checked too: each must be the restaurant's own page. Nothing is ranked by review ratings.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, and some close for part of the summer or after a storm, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency, the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation. MICHELIN and the MICHELIN Guide are trademarks of Michelin. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Florida DBPR public records and Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Florida Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Florida. Its focus is the state's food traditions: Cuban sandwiches and coffee windows, stone crabs, grouper sandwiches, Keys classics, oyster bars and Old Florida fish camps. 252 places on its guides, plus 217 MICHELIN and James Beard honorees, were checked by hand in October 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source (the restaurant's own website or menu, local news, or an official tourism listing). It also lists 52,573 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries statewide, with the State of Florida's own inspection result for 48,584 licensed places. It is for Florida residents and visitors deciding where to eat. It shows sourced facts and the state's records, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → any guide card (Cuban & Cafecito, Stone Crabs, Oyster Bars, Inspections...) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("cuban sandwich tampa", "stone crab").
- The Map tab shows the guides as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). About lists sources, licenses and the independence statement. On iPad a sidebar replaces the tabs.
- Location: if you're outside Florida (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Florida, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "FL Eats" is the short Home Screen name of "Florida Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Core Spotlight: on-device indexing so places appear in iPhone search.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation's public records (food service licenses, inspections and emergency closure reports, published under Chapter 119, Florida Statutes); Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0, with Foursquare-sourced records under Apache 2.0 and AllThePlaces under CC0; license texts are in the app); the MICHELIN Guide Florida 2026 selection and James Beard Foundation award records (facts only); and our own research of restaurants' public websites, menus and local news.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/florida-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Florida; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit, under Apple's terms; the app stores no ratings or reviews. Inspection results are shown exactly as the State of Florida records them (its disposition, its own result group and its violation counts, with dates); Florida doesn't grade restaurants and the app computes no grade. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency, the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation.
